To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the linker sequence of AraC protein is an alpha-helix in the repressing form of the protein, and (ii) the transition from the repress to the inducing form of the protein is accompanied by a transition from a helical to a nonhelical linker sequence.

the linker of AraC is helical when the protein is repressing and nonhelical when the protein induces, and that the helicity of the AraC linker is controlled by the stability or rigicity of the linker.

the behavior of the interdomain helical linker of AraC protein shifts from that of a helix to that of a nonhelical form, upon the binding or nonbinding of arabinose; the helical behavior of the linker is controlled by the stability or rigity of the linker; and, the stability of the linker is regulated by arabinose.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the control of the helical behavior of the interdomain link of the AraC protein.
the role of the interdomain linkers in controlling the repressing and inducing states of AraC protein.
how a protein changes conformation to perform a biological function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the interdomain linker of AraC undergoes a transition from an alpha-helical to a flexible nonhelix conformation in the presence of arabinone, thereby shifting the repressing AraC dimer into the inducing state.
the interdomain linker of AraC is a helix that is stabilized by residues preceding the linker sequence.
, in the absence of L-arabinose, the linker sequence in AraC adopts a helical form, and that in its presence, the linker sequence adopts a nonhelical form.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AraC protein is a molecular switch that shifts from an alpha-helical state in the repressing form to a flexible state in the inducing form.

the interdomain linker of AraC protein is an alpha-helical polypeptide that is converted to a nonhelical conformation upon the binding of the effector molecule, arabinose, and that this conformational transition is a critical event in the induction of the araBAD operon.
the helical linker sequence of AraC protein is a key element for the regulation of transcription.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interdomain linker of the AraC protein is helical in the repressing conformation of AraC and nonhelical in the inducing conformation.

the interdomain linker of AraC is helical in the absence of the inducer and nonhelical in the presence of the inducer, and that the linker's helicity is a key factor in the control of AraC's function as a repressor or an activator of transcription.
the helical behavior of a protein domain can be used to shift the equilibrium of a protein between different functional states.
